channel.title: Killed by AI — The AI Graveyard
channel.description: A digital cemetery for discontinued AI models, apps, startups, and hardware.

item.title: OpenAI GPT-5.4-Cyber — Killed by OpenAI (2026-10-01)
item.description: The 'cyber-permissive' GPT-5.4 variant built for vetted security defenders — the model that could reverse-engineer binaries and anchored OpenAI's Trusted Access for Cyber program — was shut down October 1 after five and a half months, with three weeks' notice. OpenAI's replacement advice: 'the most capable cyber model available to you.'

item.title: Mistral Leanstral 1.5 — Killed by Mistral (2026-09-30)
item.description: Mistral's Lean 4 formal-proof model was retired on September 30, exactly as its own launch note promised: 'We released Leanstral 1.5... This model will be retired on September 30, 2026.' A 92-day advertised lifespan, announced in the same sentence as its birth, with no replacement named.

item.title: Amazon Mechanical Turk — Killed by Amazon (2026-09-30)
item.description: The marketplace Jeff Bezos called "artificial artificial intelligence" closed on September 30 after 21 years — the human crowd, 500,000 strong at its peak, that labelled a generation of AI training data. Amazon shut SageMaker Ground Truth and Amazon Augmented AI the same day, leaving human-data work entirely. The official reason was an internal review of its programs; the obvious one is that the models MTurk workers trained now do MTurk's work.

item.title: Amazon Nova Canvas & Nova Reel — Killed by Amazon (2026-09-30)
item.description: The image and video half of Amazon's first Nova generation, launched at re:Invent 2024, left Bedrock on September 30 — two weeks after Nova Premier and Sonic. AWS pointed image users to Nova 2 Lite and video users to a rival's model, Luma Ray v2.

item.title: Gemini Omni Flash Preview — Killed by Google (2026-09-30)
item.description: Google's text-and-image-to-video preview shipped June 30 and was shut down September 30 — a 92-day life. Its deprecation was posted on August 27, the same day gemini-omni-1.1-flash went GA.

item.title: OpenAI davinci-002, babbage-002 & gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct — Killed by OpenAI (2026-09-28)
item.description: The end of the GPT-3 base-model lineage, retired September 28. The three shipped in August 2023, inherited the job when the original ada/babbage/curie/davinci died in January 2024, and were the last models served over the legacy /v1/completions endpoint. OpenAI's suggested replacement is gpt-5.6-terra; their fine-tuned versions outlive them by 25 days.

item.title: Reve AI Image Generation — Killed by OpenAI (2026-09-27)
item.description: Reve's image generator — briefly the top-ranked text-to-image model on launch in March 2025 — shut off at noon Pacific on September 27, the price of an investment from OpenAI, which also took its AI research team to lead multimodal work. The API went dark on August 14 and sign-ups stopped September 17; users have until October 31 to export, and September fees are refunded. The company survives; the product does not.

item.title: GM Cruise — Killed by General Motors (2024-12-10)
item.description: The robotaxi startup GM bought in 2016 and then poured more than $10 billion into, with Honda ($852M), Microsoft and SoftBank alongside. Driverless paid rides began in San Francisco in 2022; a 2023 crash in which a Cruise car dragged a pedestrian, and the company's handling of it, cost it its California permit. In December 2024 Mary Barra ended the program, citing the 'incremental time and capital' still needed. The most expensive AI product death on record.

item.title: Forward (CarePods) — Killed by Itself (2024-11-12)
item.description: A primary-care startup that raised $657M on the promise of AI-run doctor's offices, culminating in 'CarePods' — self-serve kiosks meant to automate check-ups. Only three pods ever launched, one was pulled soon after installation, and former staff described patients getting stuck inside. Forward shut down in November 2024 with a few weeks' notice.

item.title: Ghost Autonomy — Killed by Market (2024-04-03)
item.description: A self-driving software startup that raised about $220M and, months before closing, landed an investment from OpenAI's startup fund to bring large language models to autonomous driving. It shut down worldwide on April 3, 2024, unable to secure the long-term funding its plan required.

item.title: Embark Trucks — Killed by Market (2023-03-03)
item.description: An autonomous-trucking company that went public via SPAC in 2021 and raised more than $400 million. With no revenue and capital markets closed to pre-revenue companies, it cut 70% of staff and began liquidating its self-driving truck assets in March 2023. Its timeline for driverless freight never arrived; the money did run out.

item.title: Argo AI — Killed by Ford & Volkswagen (2022-10-26)
item.description: Pittsburgh's self-driving champion, backed by roughly $1 billion from Ford and $2.6 billion from Volkswagen. Six years in, both backers decided that fully driverless cars were further away than they could keep paying for, declined to invest further, and absorbed its assets. Around 2,000 employees were offered jobs at the two carmakers; the company itself simply stopped.

item.title: MAI-Transcribe-1 (Microsoft Foundry) — Killed by Microsoft (2026-09-15)
item.description: Microsoft's first-party speech model, version 2026-01-23, retired from Foundry on September 15 — less than eight months old, replaced by MAI-Transcribe-1.5. The same accelerated churn that took MAI-Image-2 at 176 days and MAI-Code-1-Flash at 100.

item.title: theGist — Killed by Itself (2026-09-15)
item.description: An Israeli startup that scanned Slack, email, CRM and analytics to hand each employee a personalised summary of what mattered — founded in 2022 by alumni of Wix, Blizzard, OpenWeb and Gong, with $7M pre-seed co-led by StageOne and Aleph. A pivot toward sales tooling never caught, and rather than spend the remainder the founders closed the company and returned the money to investors. ⚠ Closure reported mid-September 2026; no exact date was published.

item.title: Amazon Nova Premier & Nova Sonic — Killed by Amazon (2026-09-14)
item.description: Amazon's flagship Nova model and its speech sibling, launched at re:Invent 2024 as AWS's answer to frontier models. Both entered Legacy status in March 2026 and reached end of life on September 14 — inside two years. AWS migrated nothing automatically; Legacy models also cut off any customer inactive for 15 days, so some accounts lost access before the deadline arrived.

item.title: Huxe — Killed by Google / Spotify (2026-05-22)
item.description: An AI audio app from three former NotebookLM developers — prompt it and get a podcast, a personalised feed, or a live AI radio station you could interrupt mid-sentence. It raised $4.6M from Conviction, Dylan Field and Google's own Jeff Dean. Spotify shipped a near-identical personal podcast feature one day before the wind-down notice, and Google's Gemini Daily Brief had landed at I/O weeks earlier. Built by ex-Googlers, buried by Google.

item.title: Figgs AI — Killed by Inference Bills (2024-12-30)
item.description: A character-chat platform for role-play and storytelling that reached more than a million users on a free tier, with no funding and no revenue at any point. Character chat is among the most expensive things to serve per user, and the developers shut it down at the end of 2024 rather than charge for it. Demand was never the problem; the bill was.

item.title: MAI-Code-1-Flash (GitHub Copilot) — Killed by GitHub / Microsoft (2026-09-10)
item.description: Microsoft's first purpose-built small coding model for GitHub Copilot, announced June 2, 2026 as "the first in a new wave" of Copilot-tuned models. On August 11 GitHub shipped MAI-Code-1.1-Flash (with vision) and, in the same day's changelog, put 1.0 on notice; it was removed from every Copilot surface on September 10. One hundred days from launch to retirement — the first wave lasted about as long as a summer.

item.title: Gemini Robotics-ER 1.6 Preview — Killed by Google (2026-08-31)
item.description: Released April 14, 2026, deleted August 31: a 139-day lifespan for an embodied-reasoning model that never left preview. It had killed its own predecessor, ER 1.5, on April 30, and was in turn replaced by gemini-robotics-er-2-preview, which shipped July 30 — 32 days before 1.6 was gone. Three robotics previews retired inside five months, none of which ever reached GA.

item.title: Mistral Medium 3 & 3.1 — Killed by Mistral (2026-08-31)
item.description: Both retired the same day, August 31, 2026, in favour of Mistral Medium 3.5. Medium 3 shipped May 7, 2025 and lasted 481 days; Medium 3.1 shipped August 12, 2025 and managed 384. Both were marked deprecated on May 22, so developers got 101 days' notice — generous by 2026 standards, where some previews don't live that long.

item.title: Flowise — Killed by AI Coding Agents (2026-08-31)
item.description: The open-source drag-and-drop LLM builder with 55,000 GitHub stars froze feature development on July 29, 2026, archived the repository on August 13 and declared end of life on August 31. Maintainer HenryHengZJ was candid about the cause: "the typical rigid workflow low-code approach quickly hits the limit when it comes to complexity" as developers hand complex work to coding agents instead. A tool for building AI without code, killed by AI that writes code. The Apache-2.0 source stays up for forks.

item.title: DALL·E GPT (in ChatGPT) — Killed by OpenAI (2026-08-30)
item.description: The official DALL·E GPT — the last place the DALL·E name still lived inside ChatGPT — retired on August 30, 2026, 1,028 days after it launched alongside custom GPTs at DevDay 2023. OpenAI would not say what happens to images stored inside it and simply advised users to download anything they wanted to keep. Image generation itself survives under the ChatGPT Images banner. Three DALL·E entries now share this graveyard.

item.title: OpenAI Assistants API — Killed by OpenAI (2026-08-26)
item.description: OpenAI's first stab at agents-as-a-service: threads, runs, file search and code interpreter bundled behind one beta endpoint. Announced at DevDay on November 6, 2023, it never left beta, and on August 26, 2025 OpenAI gave it exactly one year to live. It died on the day — a hard cut, no read-only mode, no grace period — with the Responses API inheriting its best parts and developers inheriting a full rewrite. 1,024 days, every one of them labelled "beta".

item.title: Claude 3 Haiku on Google Cloud — Killed by Google Cloud (2026-08-23)
item.description: Deprecated on Google Cloud on February 23, 2026 and switched off on August 23 — the last Claude 3-generation model on the platform. Anthropic itself had retired claude-3-haiku on April 20, so Google kept serving a model its maker had already buried for 125 extra days. Amazon Bedrock, not to be outdone, keeps it on life support until September 10: one model, three funerals.

item.title: HereAfter AI — Killed by Itself (2026-08-18)
item.description: The grief-tech pioneer that interviewed people about their lives so relatives could later ask questions and hear answers in the recorded voice — built by former journalist James Vlahos from the 'Dadbot' he made of his dying father. Vlahos left in January 2024; the iOS app was last updated in September 2023. A farewell notice appeared on the homepage in July 2026 with no deadline, telling families to email support to export recordings; by August 18 the site itself no longer loaded. ⚠ The closing date here is the day the site went dark, as no official end date was published.

item.title: Anthropic Legacy Workbench — Killed by Anthropic (2026-08-17)
item.description: Announced July 17, 2026 and gone August 17, the legacy Console Workbench took its saved prompts, variables and evals with it — none migrated to the replacement "playground" that opened a day later. The three experimental prompt-tool endpoints (generate_prompt, improve_prompt, templatize_prompt) were retired the same day and now return errors. Thirty-one days' notice for an API that was, to be fair, always labelled experimental.

item.title: Microsoft MAI-Image-2 & MAI-Image-2e — Killed by Microsoft (2026-08-15)
item.description: Microsoft's first in-house image models did not get long. MAI-Image-2 (February 20) and MAI-Image-2e (April 9) were retired from Azure Foundry on August 15, 2026 — 176 and 128 days after release — in favour of MAI-Image-2.5 and 2.5-Flash. The successors are still in preview and already carry their own retirement date of October 1. Microsoft is now deprecating image models faster than most companies ship them.

item.title: Wsup AI — Killed by Itself (2026-06-19)
item.description: A no-sign-up AI character-chat app that briefly found an audience in the gap beneath Character.AI and Replika. In May 2026 it announced a wind-down: chats worked until May 24, accounts went read-only from May 25, and the service closed on June 19. No reason was given beyond the obvious one — an 18-month-old companion app cannot outspend incumbents with multi-year head starts. An unrelated operator has since launched a look-alike under the same name.

item.title: Weights (weights.gg) — Killed by OpenAI (2026-03-31)
item.description: The community voice-cloning and AI-music platform where thousands of celebrity and character voice models lived. Weights announced in January 2026 that it had never been profitable and closed on March 31; two months later The New York Times reported that OpenAI had quietly bought its technology and roughly six engineers. Its library of consent-free celebrity voices had become a liability as deepfake laws tightened — the thing that made it popular was the thing that made it unsellable as a product.

item.title: Cohere Command R & Command R+ on Amazon Bedrock — Killed by AWS (2026-08-19)
item.description: The RAG-and-tool-use pair AWS launched on Bedrock in April 2024 both hit end-of-life at 08:00 UTC, after a staged wind-down: legacy in February, new customers cut off in May, hard kill in August. AWS named no replacement for either. Cohere had already pulled the originals from its own API back in September 2025 — along with command-light, base command, summarize, and its entire fine-tuning product.
